newsitem.title: USA: Germany's DTB plans to hold its own in face of EMU.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DTB plans to hold its own in face of EMU.

text.p: Germany's futures and options exchange Deutsche Terminboerse (DTB) expects to hold its own in the face of more competition linked to European monetary union, general manager Joerg Franke said Thursday.

Franke told a news conference the electronic bourse's array of remote access sites enables more competition and cost effective trading that will remain attractive long after the planned January 1999 union.
DTB has access sites in Amsterdam, London, Paris and Zurich, and a fifth external site in Chicago was officially launched Thursday.
The access sites allow investors outside Germany to trade various German futures and options.
Franke added that the electronic trading system allows for efficient increases in capacity and helps keep transaction costs down.
Transaction costs at the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) run two to five percent higher than at the DTB, he said.

"The race for the Euro is on," Franke said, adding that futures exchanges have two main tasks -- seamlessly switching existing products to new ones and developing new products as existing ones become less important.
New stock indices are likely to emerge that will represent industry sectors and combine shares traded across Europe, Franke said.
Obvious examples include the chemical industry and the auto industry, he said.
"We think this will be the future of indices," he said.
The DTB's focus is on products based on interest rates, but "the equity side is interesting," he said.
